name: application-body-metrics-card
title: Body Metrics Card
description: Body metrics card with weight, BMI, and body fat cells, each showing a trend arrow whose direction and color are computed from a real signed delta.
useWhen: Showing a health/fitness dashboard summary of a user's most recent body measurements.
Each metric benefits from a trend indicator showing change since the last reading, not just the current value.
Different metrics have different "good" directions (e.g. weight down is good for a loss goal, but up is good for a gain goal) and the trend color should reflect that.
avoidWhen: You need general vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure) rather than body composition metrics — use `vitals-stat-row` for that clinical framing instead.
There's no historical comparison available — drop the trend arrows and show plain values rather than fabricating a direction.
This is used for clinical diagnosis or medical decision-making — this is a consumer fitness-tracking UI pattern, not a substitute for validated medical device software.
responsiveBehavior: Three-column grid with dividers; each cell's text wraps rather than overflowing at narrow card widths.
accessibility: Trend direction (up/down arrow) and color (good/bad) are both computed from the same signed delta and a per-metric increaseIsGood flag, so they can never disagree with each other.
"Good" vs. "concerning" trends are distinguished by icon direction and color together, with the numeric delta always shown as text — not color alone.
Each metric's label, value, and delta are all real text content, remaining fully readable to screen readers.

variants.title: Body Metrics Card
variants.description: Weight and BMI trending down (shown as good/green), body fat trending up and flagged red as an undesirable change.
accessibility: Trend arrow direction and good/bad color are both derived from the same real delta value per metric.

variants.title: Body Metrics Card (Dark)
variants.description: Body metrics card adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Trend colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
